sequence: Immutable current baseline and complete open/draft work inventory
Risk-ranked static review with exact authored-path/function coverage
Bounded reproduction, finding deduplication and supervisor disposition
Owner fixes with maintained regression tests and independent review
One coordinated release window in dependency order, registry provenance verification and site adoption
Focused production verification and final coverage/risk report
coverageRules: Read authored first-party runtime, scripts, tests, current examples/docs, workflows and configuration; record reviewed paths rather than infer coverage from test results.
Inventory generated data and binary/vendor artifacts separately; review generators and wrappers, verify identities and explicitly describe sampling/exclusions.
Review every authorization boundary and open/draft PR on its own immutable head.
Retain source, packed, registry, browser and native evidence as separate claims; preserve every initial failure.
Keep private-site code/findings out of public evidence; the supervisor retains the private combined ledger.
acceptance: Every agreed unit has explicit evidence and supervisor acceptance; no unexplained authored-code exclusions.
Every confirmed finding has a fix or an explicit reasoned disposition; critical/high fixes receive independent review.
Approved documentation changes use authoritative APIs/current setup data and preserve truthful released-versus-candidate boundaries.
Required normal checks pass without weaker gates/tolerances.
Release only changed/required packages through merged-source trusted publishing; verify each registry artifact/provenance before site adoption.
Record actual source/artifact/deployment identity and residual risk; no global/native certification is inferred.
nativeBoundary: Review agents do not operate Office or change fonts. Existing supervisor/owner native-host boundaries remain unchanged.
publicSiteBoundary: This repository tracker does not add public support/readiness badges, status panels or new status APIs to the three sites.
